Where each installed package came from

Source: R/upgrade_r_library.R
installed_pkg_sources.Rd

Classifies the installed (non-base, non-recommended) packages in a library by where they were installed from, using the Repository and Remote* fields that install.packages(), remotes/devtools and pak record in each package's DESCRIPTION. This is what upgrade_r_library() and restore_installed_pkgs() use to reinstall packages from the right place.

Usage

installed_pkg_sources(lib.loc = NULL)

Arguments

lib.loc

library directories to look in; default: all of .libPaths()

Value

A data frame, one row per package, with columns

  • Package, Version

  • Built: the R version the package was built under

  • source: one of

    • "cran": from CRAN

    • "repo": from another CRAN-like repository, such as an r-universe (URL in spec)

    • "rforge": from R-Forge

    • "bioc": from Bioconductor

    • "github", "gitlab", ...: from a remote, via remotes/devtools/pak (spec is user/repo, or user/repo/subdir)

    • "local": from a local source or zip file; cannot be reinstalled automatically

    • "obsolete": built under R < 4.0.0, so it cannot be loaded by a current R

    • "skip": not an installable package (the translations folder that R itself ships)

  • spec: what to install from, for the repo and remote sources

  • LibPath: the library the package is in

See also

upgrade_r_library(), save_installed_pkgs()

Examples

src <- installed_pkg_sources()
table(src$source)
#> 
#>     cran   github    local obsolete     repo   rforge     skip 
#>     1040       11        3        2        2        1        1 
subset(src, source != "cran")
